summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with long-standing epilepsy, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of stroke, was admitted after experiencing a generalized tonic-clonic seizure following a hemodialysis session. The seizure occurred in the context of significant fluid removal (4.5 L), post-dialysis hypotension (SBP 75), fasting for a scheduled colonoscopy, and failure to take his usual extra doses of oxcarbazepine and levetiracetam after dialysis. He had another witnessed seizure in the emergency department, which resolved with intravenous lorazepam. Evaluation included a CT head and chest X-ray, both showing no acute abnormalities. He received the missed antiepileptic doses and 500 mL of IV fluids. His condition stabilized, mental status returned to baseline, and he was discharged home after two days. Medications were continued without change, and he was advised to follow up with his neurologist and dialysis team, with emphasis on medication adherence, especially post-dialysis doses.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
